question.knowledge_point: Estimating a Derivative From a Graph Using a Forward Difference Approximation: Word Problem
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14057748/assets/4a7e89a828cbd660357d4834e0bcb9cb5c316dbe24419865206ba5f41872963d.png)

The power of a mobile phone emitter increases when the phone is switched on. The power output of the emitter after $t$ minutes is given by $W(t),$ where $W$ is measured in watts. The graph of $W(t)$ is shown above. 
Approximate the rate of increase in the power of the emitter when $t=1$ using a forward difference approximation with step size $h=2.$
question.worked_solution:
We use the forward difference approximation

$$
{W}^{′}(t)≈\frac{W(t+h)-W(t)}{h},
$$

 
at the time $t=1$ with step size $h=2.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{W}^{′}(1) & ≈\frac{W(1+2)-W(1)}{2} \\  & =\frac{W(3)-W(1)}{2} \\  & =\frac{100-50}{2} \\  & =25.\end{aligned}
$$

So, after $1$ minute, the power is increasing at a rate of approximately $25\,\text{watts}/\text{minute}.$
